prompt: An engineer studying an AC circuit meets the expression $1 - 2\sin^2(\omega t)$. Which single trig function is it equal to?
hint: The cosine double-angle formula comes in three equivalent versions.

hints.text: The cosine double-angle formula comes in three equivalent versions.
One of them is $\cos(2\theta) = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta$. Compare it with what you have.
With $\theta = \omega t$ the expression is exactly $\cos(2\omega t)$.

explanation: The three forms of the cosine double-angle identity are $\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta$, $2\cos^2\theta - 1$, and $1 - 2\sin^2\theta$.
The expression matches the third form with $\theta = \omega t$.
So $1 - 2\sin^2(\omega t) = \cos(2\omega t)$ — this is exactly how engineers show that the power in an AC circuit oscillates at twice the supply frequency.

alternativeExplanations.title: Derive it if you forget it
steps: That simplifies to $1 - 2\sin^2\theta$ — you never have to memorise all three separately.
